page: Amazon Web Services t2.micro is an entry-level burstable instance within the general-purpose family, deployed on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz on an i386 architecture. The instance allocates a single burstable vCPU backed by one physical core with one thread, alongside 1.0 GB of system memory. It does not include integrated hardware accelerators or local instance storage, relying entirely on remote volumes for persistent storage.

Performance metrics place this instance in the lower tiers across synthetic benchmarks due to its constrained hardware profile and credit-based execution model. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core evaluations both recorded 157.0, placing it within the bottom 10 percent of tested configurations. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 10.85 GB/sec for uncached reads and 7.0 GB/sec for writes. PassMark tests yielded an overall CPU score of 1438.31 and a memory score of 755.64. In operational tests, the configuration achieved 0.51 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads and 1.12 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

From an efficiency perspective, the profile offers a lightweight resource footprint for workloads that remain mostly idle or require only intermittent compute cycles. The primary tradeoff centers on performance throttling once accumulated CPU burst credits are exhausted, combined with a 0 Gbps baseline network rating and the absence of bundled local storage. As a result, the instance is appropriate for low-traffic web applications, minimal administrative jump hosts, small development environments, and low-throughput background microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services t2.micro is a budget burstable virtual server built on the Xen hypervisor, designed for intermittent compute needs. The instance provides 1 vCPU and 1.0 GB of system memory driven by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2676 v3 processor using the i386 architecture. There are no attached GPUs or local storage drives, requiring networked storage volumes for disk operations, while network throughput operates with a baseline rating of 0 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reflect its low-resource profile, recording 157.0 in stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 1438.31. Memory throughput reaches 10.85 GB/sec for read operations and 7.0 GB/sec for writes on large blocks, with operational benchmarks reporting 0.51 million Redis SET operations per second. Consequently, this server profile is best matched to entry-level testing environments, low-traffic web hosting, jump boxes, and modest utility processes that do not experience sustained computational demand.
